nodes.summary: For an integer flow matrix $f$ on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$, its arc flow is the natural-number matrix whose entry at $(u, v)$ is the positive part $\max(f(u, v), 0)$ of $f(u, v)$.
nodes.title: Arc flow of an integer flow

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $s$ and $t$ be vertices, and let $f$ be a flow that is feasible for $c$, $s$, $t$. Let $P = (v_0, \dots, v_k)$ be a nonempty list of pairwise distinct vertices with $v_0 = s$ and $v_k = t$, and let $a$ be an integer with $0 \le a$ and $a \le c(v_i, v_{i+1}) - f(v_i, v_{i+1})$ for every $i < k$. Then the augmentation of…
nodes.title: Augmentation within residual capacities preserves feasibility

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $s$ and $t$ be vertices, and let $f$ be a flow that is feasible for $c$, $s$, $t$. If $P$ is a path from $s$ to $t$ in the residual graph of $f$, that is, a nonempty list of pairwise distinct vertices starting at $s$ and ending at $t$ whose consecutive pairs are residual edges, then the augmentation of $f$ along $P$ by…
nodes.title: Bottleneck augmentation preserves feasibility

nodes.summary: Given an integer flow matrix $f$ on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, a list of vertices $P$ and an integer $a$, the augmentation of $f$ along $P$ by $a$ is the matrix whose entry at $(u, v)$ is $f(u, v) + a \cdot d$, where $d$ is the number of consecutive pairs of $P$ equal to $(u, v)$ minus the number of consecutive pairs of $P$ equal to $(v, u)$, counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Augmenting a flow along a path

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $s$ and $t$ be vertices, and let $f$ be a flow that is feasible for $c$, $s$, $t$. Then for all vertices $u$ and $v$, we have $-c(v, u) \le f(u, v) \le c(u, v)$.
nodes.title: Two-sided capacity bounds for a feasible flow

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity function on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ with natural-number values, viewed as real capacities, and let $s \ne t$ be vertices. Let $S_0$ be the set of vertices reachable from $s$ in the residual graph of the flow computed by the Edmonds–Karp algorithm on $c$, $s$, $t$. Then for every $s$-$t$ cut $S$, the capacity of $S_0$ is at most the capacity of $S$.
nodes.title: No $s$-$t$ cut is smaller than the Edmonds–Karp residual cut

nodes.summary: For a capacity matrix $c$ with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a set $S$ of vertices, the capacity of the cut $S$ is the integer $\sum_{u \in S} \sum_{v \notin S} c(u, v)$.
nodes.title: Cut capacity

nodes.summary: For a list $P$ of elements of a set $V$ and elements $u, v$ of $V$, the edge delta of $P$ at $(u, v)$ is the integer obtained as the number of consecutive pairs of $P$ equal to $(u, v)$ minus the number of consecutive pairs of $P$ equal to $(v, u)$, counted with multiplicity. It is $0$ when $P$ has fewer than two elements.
nodes.title: Edge delta of a path

nodes.summary: For every capacity matrix $c$ with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and all vertices $s$ and $t$, the flow $f$ returned by the Edmonds–Karp algorithm on $c$, $s$, $t$ is feasible for $c$, $s$, $t$: it is skew-symmetric, satisfies $f(u, v) \le c(u, v)$ for all vertices $u, v$, and has zero net outflow at every vertex other than $s$ and $t$.
nodes.title: The Edmonds–Karp flow is feasible

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity function on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ with natural-number values, viewed as real capacities, and let $s \ne t$ be vertices. Let $f$ be the real arc flow of the flow computed by the Edmonds-Karp algorithm on $c$, $s$, $t$ (its positive part, viewed as real numbers), and let $S_0$ be the set of vertices reachable from $s$ in the residual graph of that flow. Then $f$ is a feasible $s$-$t$ flow…
nodes.title: Edmonds-Karp computes a maximum flow and a minimum cut

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $s$ and $t$ be distinct vertices, and let $f$ be the flow returned by the Edmonds–Karp algorithm on $c$, $s$, $t$. Then every integer flow $g$ that is feasible for $c$, $s$, $t$ has value at $s$ at most the value of $f$ at $s$, where the value of a flow at $s$ is its net flow out of $s$.
nodes.title: Maximality of the Edmonds–Karp flow

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $s$ and $t$ be distinct vertices, and let $f$ be the flow returned by the Edmonds–Karp algorithm on $c$, $s$, $t$. Then the net flow of $f$ out of $s$ equals the capacity of the cut formed by the vertices reachable from $s$ in the residual graph of $f$.
nodes.title: The Edmonds–Karp flow value equals its residual cut capacity

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $s$ and $t$ be distinct vertices. Then $t$ is not reachable from $s$ in the residual graph of the flow returned by the Edmonds–Karp algorithm on $c$, $s$, $t$.
nodes.title: No augmenting path remains after Edmonds–Karp

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity function assigning a natural number $c(u, v)$ to each ordered pair of vertices, and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices. If $s = t$, the Edmonds–Karp flow is the zero flow. Otherwise it is the result of running at most $C + 1$ rounds of bottleneck augmentation from the zero flow, where $C = \sum_v c(s, v)$ is the total capacity leaving $s$: each round looks for a shortest path from $s$ to $t$ in the…
nodes.title: Edmonds–Karp maximum flow

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity function on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ with natural-number values, viewed as real capacities, and let $s \ne t$ be vertices. Then there is a natural-number valued function $f$ on pairs of vertices which, viewed as a real function, is a feasible $s$-$t$ flow for $c$ whose value is at least the value of every feasible real-valued $s$-$t$ flow for $c$.
nodes.title: Integral flow theorem

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be an integer flow matrix on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ that is skew-symmetric, $f(u, v) = -f(v, u)$ for all $u, v$, and let $a(u, v) = \max(f(u, v), 0)$ be its arc flow. Then $f(u, v) = a(u, v) - a(v, u)$ for all vertices $u$ and $v$.
nodes.title: A skew flow is the difference of its arc flows

nodes.summary: Let $s \ne t$ be vertices, $f$ a flow, $a$ an integer, and $p$ a nonempty list of vertices whose first entry is $s$ and whose last entry is $t$. Then the net flow leaving $s$ under the flow obtained by augmenting $f$ along $p$ by $a$ equals the net flow leaving $s$ under $f$, plus $a$.
nodes.title: Augmenting along a path changes the flow value by the amount

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity function, $s$ and $t$ vertices, and $f$ a flow that is feasible for $c$, $s$ and $t$. For every set $S$ of vertices with $s \in S$ and $t \notin S$, the net flow leaving $s$ under $f$ is at most the capacity of the cut $S$, namely $\sum_{u \in S} \sum_{v \notin S} c(u, v)$.
nodes.title: Weak max-flow min-cut duality

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity function and $s \ne t$ vertices. For every flow $f$ and every natural number $k$, the net flow leaving $s$ after running at most $k$ rounds of bottleneck augmentation from $f$ is at least the net flow leaving $s$ under $f$.
nodes.title: The augmentation loop never decreases the flow value

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity function, $s$ and $t$ vertices, and $f$ a flow that is feasible for $c$, $s$ and $t$. Then the net flow leaving $s$ under $f$ is at most $\sum_v c(s, v)$, the total capacity leaving $s$.
nodes.title: The flow value is at most the source capacity

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity function and $s \ne t$ vertices. For every flow $f$, the flow obtained from $f$ by one step of bottleneck augmentation either has the same net flow leaving $s$ as $f$, or a strictly larger one.
nodes.title: One augmentation step keeps or strictly raises the flow value

nodes.summary: For a flow $f$ on $n$ vertices and a vertex $s$, the value of $f$ at $s$ is the net flow leaving $s$, namely the integer $\sum_v f(s, v)$, where $v$ runs over all vertices.
nodes.title: Flow value

nodes.summary: A flow on $n$ vertices, labelled $0, \dots, n-1$, is an integer matrix: it assigns an integer $f(u, v)$ to each ordered pair of vertices $(u, v)$.
nodes.title: Flow

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity function on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ with natural-number values and let $s, t$ be vertices. If an integer flow matrix $f$ is a feasible skew-symmetric $s$-$t$ flow for $c$, then its arc flow $(u, v) \mapsto \max(f(u, v), 0)$, viewed as a real function, is a feasible $s$-$t$ flow for $c$ viewed as real capacities.
nodes.title: A feasible skew flow gives a feasible flow

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity function assigning a natural number $c(u, v)$ to each ordered pair of vertices, and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices. A flow $f$ is feasible for $c$, $s$ and $t$ when it is skew symmetric, $f(u, v) = -f(v, u)$ for all $u$ and $v$; it respects the capacities, $f(u, v) \le c(u, v)$ for all $u$ and $v$; and it is conserved: for every vertex $v$ other than $s$ and $t$, the net flow $\sum_w f(v, w)$…
nodes.title: Feasible flow

nodes.summary: In a directed graph $G$, a list $p$ of vertices is a path from $s$ to $t$ when it is nonempty, its first entry is $s$, its last entry is $t$, every pair of consecutive entries $u, v$ forms a directed edge of $G$ from $u$ to $v$, and no vertex occurs twice in $p$.
nodes.title: Directed path

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity function on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ with natural-number values and let $s \ne t$ be vertices. The set of vertices reachable from $s$ in the residual graph of the flow computed by the Edmonds-Karp algorithm on $c$, $s$, $t$ is an $s$-$t$ cut: it contains $s$ and not $t$.
nodes.title: The Edmonds-Karp residual cut separates source and sink

nodes.summary: For vertices $a$, $b$, $u$, $v$, the unit skew flow of the oriented edge $(a, b)$ at the ordered pair $(u, v)$ is the integer $[u = a \text{ and } v = b] - [u = b \text{ and } v = a]$, where $[P]$ is $1$ if $P$ holds and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Unit skew flow along an oriented edge

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries and $f$ any integer matrix (the flow) on the vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$, and let $s \ne t$ be vertices. If $p$ is a duplicate-free path from $s$ to $t$ in the residual graph of $c$ and $f$, then the bottleneck of $p$, the minimum of $c(u, v) - f(u, v)$ over consecutive vertices $u, v$ of $p$, is positive.
nodes.title: Augmenting paths have positive bottleneck

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries and $f$ an integer matrix (the flow) on the same vertices. The bottleneck of a list of vertices $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_k$ with $k \ge 1$ is the integer $\min_{i < k} \bigl(c(v_i, v_{i+1}) - f(v_i, v_{i+1})\bigr)$, the least residual capacity of a consecutive pair; a list with at most one vertex has bottleneck $0$.
nodes.title: Bottleneck of a path

nodes.summary: The edges of a list $v_0, v_1, \dots, v_k$ are the list of its consecutive ordered pairs $(v_0, v_1), (v_1, v_2), \dots, (v_{k-1}, v_k)$, in this order; the empty list and one-element lists have no edges.
nodes.title: Edges of a path

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed adjacency graph on a type $V$ whose Boolean test $\equiv$ on pairs of vertices holds exactly for equal vertices, let $d$ be a partial labelling of the vertices by natural numbers, let $t$ and $u$ be vertices, and let $k$ be a natural number. If the distance-guided reconstruction for $G$, $d$ and $t$ from $u$ with $k$ steps left succeeds and returns a list $p$, then $p$ is a walk from $u$ to…
nodes.title: Soundness of distance-guided path reconstruction

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a directed graph with ordered adjacency lists, $d$ a partial labelling of its vertices by natural numbers, $t$ a vertex, and $\equiv$ a given Boolean test on pairs of vertices (not required to be equality). The reconstruction from a vertex $u$ with $k$ steps left returns the one-element list $[u]$ when $k = 0$ and $u \equiv t$ holds, and fails when $k = 0$ and $u \equiv t$ fails. When $k \ge 1$, it takes…
nodes.title: Distance-guided path reconstruction

nodes.summary: For a capacity function $c$ on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$ with natural-number values, the real capacities are the same values viewed as real numbers, $(u, v) \mapsto c(u, v) \in \mathbb{R}$.
nodes.title: Real capacities

nodes.summary: For an integer flow matrix $f$ on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$, its real arc flow is the function $(u, v) \mapsto \max(f(u, v), 0)$, the arc flow of $f$, viewed as real numbers.
nodes.title: Real arc flow

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries and $f$ an integer matrix (the flow) on the vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$. The residual capacity of an ordered pair of vertices $(u, v)$ is the integer $c(u, v) - f(u, v)$.
nodes.title: Residual capacity

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix assigning a natural number $c(u, v)$ to each ordered pair of vertices among $0, \dots, n - 1$, let $f$ be a flow on these vertices, and let $s$ be a vertex. The residual cut of $c$, $f$ and $s$ is the set of vertices visited by breadth-first search from $s$ in the residual graph of $c$ and $f$, that is, the set of vertices reachable from $s$ in that residual graph.
nodes.title: Residual cut

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries and $f$ an integer matrix (the flow) on the vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$. For all vertices $u$ and $v$, the residual graph of $c$ and $f$ has an edge from $u$ to $v$ if and only if $f(u, v) < c(u, v)$.
nodes.title: Edges of the residual graph

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix assigning a natural number $c(u, v)$ to each ordered pair of vertices among $0, \dots, n - 1$, and let $f$ be a flow on these vertices. The residual graph of $c$ and $f$ is the directed adjacency graph whose vertices $0, \dots, n - 1$ are enumerated in increasing order and in which the adjacency list of $u$ consists of the vertices $v$ with $f(u, v) < c(u, v)$, that is, with positive…
nodes.title: Residual graph

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, let $s$ and $t$ be vertices, and let $f$ be a flow (an integer-valued matrix on pairs of vertices). If the breadth-first shortest-path search finds no path from $s$ to $t$ in the residual graph of $f$ with respect to $c$, then for every fuel bound $k$, the augmenting-path iteration started at $f$ with fuel $k$ returns $f$.
nodes.title: The iteration stops when there is no augmenting path

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, let $s$ be a source and $t$ a sink, let $k$ be a fuel bound and let $f$ be a flow (an integer-valued matrix on pairs of vertices). The iteration returns $f$ if $k = 0$ or $s = t$. Otherwise it runs the breadth-first shortest-path search from $s$ to $t$ in the residual graph of $f$ with respect to $c$. If the search finds…
nodes.title: Augmenting-path iteration with fuel

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices. The breadth-first shortest-path search in $G$ from $s$ to $t$ returns no path if and only if $t$ is not reachable from $s$ in $G$.
nodes.title: The shortest-path search fails exactly when the sink is unreachable

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices. The breadth-first shortest-path search in $G$ from $s$ to $t$ returns some path if and only if $t$ is reachable from $s$ in $G$ (every vertex counts as reachable from itself).
nodes.title: The shortest-path search succeeds exactly when the sink is reachable

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ and let $s$ and $t$ be vertices. If the breadth-first shortest-path search in $G$ from $s$ to $t$ returns a list $P$ of vertices, then $P$ is a directed path in $G$ from $s$ to $t$ without repeated vertices, and breadth-first search in $G$ from $s$ assigns $t$ a distance $d$ such that $P$ has exactly $d + 1$ vertices.
nodes.title: Soundness of the shortest-path search

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite directed graph on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ with ordered adjacency lists, and let $s$ be a source and $t$ a sink. Run breadth-first search from $t$ in the reverse graph of $G$; it labels each vertex $v$ from which $t$ is reachable with the distance from $v$ to $t$ in $G$. If $s$ has no label, the search returns no path. Otherwise, starting at $s$ with label $d$, take $d$ steps, each…
nodes.title: Shortest path via breadth-first search

nodes.summary: For a capacity matrix $c$ with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ and a source $s$, the source capacity is the total capacity leaving $s$, namely $\sum_{v} c(s, v)$, where $v$ ranges over all vertices, including $s$ itself.
nodes.title: Source capacity

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a capacity matrix with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$, let $s$ be a source and $t$ a sink, and let $f$ be a flow (an integer-valued matrix on pairs of vertices). Run the breadth-first shortest-path search from $s$ to $t$ in the residual graph of $f$ with respect to $c$. If it finds no path, the step returns $f$. If it returns a path $P$, let $b$ be the bottleneck of $P$, the…
nodes.title: One augmenting-path step

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a skew-symmetric integer flow matrix on the vertices $0, \dots, n-1$, so $f(u, v) = -f(v, u)$ for all $u, v$, and let $a(u, v) = \max(f(u, v), 0)$ be its arc flow, viewed as real numbers. Then for every vertex $v$, $\sum_w a(v, w) - \sum_u a(u, v) = \sum_w f(v, w)$, the net flow leaving $v$.
nodes.title: Net outflow in the arc representation

nodes.summary: For every capacity matrix $c$ with natural-number entries on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ and all vertices $s$ and $t$, the zero flow is feasible for $c$ with source $s$ and sink $t$.
nodes.title: The zero flow is feasible

nodes.summary: The zero flow on the vertices $\{0, \dots, n - 1\}$ is the integer-valued matrix $f$ with $f(u, v) = 0$ for all vertices $u$ and $v$.
nodes.title: Zero flow

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
